related.note: Both describe Stephen Hawking going down in a submarine in the circle around Epstein. This telling says the dive was to look at possible Atlantis ruins, while the story says it was to study gravitational anomalies in the Bahamas basin.

plain: The financier Jeffrey Epstein took people down in submarines, the physicist Stephen Hawking among them, to study what were described as quantum gravitational anomalies in the Bahamas basin, the stretch of sea known as the Bermuda Triangle. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells Michels this, crediting others such as a researcher named Eric Weinstein, and if true it would suggest Epstein's circle was chasing ways to beat gravity. Jorjani's own article "Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell", published 29 July 2025, tells of a single dive in which Epstein's associate Ghislaine Maxwell piloted the "Atlantis" submarine that took Epstein and Hawking to the Bermuda Triangle seabed "to study quantum magnetic anomalies". That is magnetic, not gravitational, and the article does not name the Bahamas. It adds that Epstein's foundation sponsored a 2006 conference titled "Confronting Gravity" with top physicists from places like Caltech, MIT, Harvard and CERN.

discussion.by: Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell
discussion.text: The piece names one submarine dive, in the Atlantis submarine Ghislaine Maxwell piloted, that took Epstein and Stephen Hawking "down to the seabed of the Bermuda Triangle to study quantum magnetic anomalies there", the region the podcast names; it tells one dive where the podcast speaks of people taken down in submarines, and it says magnetic where the podcast says gravitational.
